study.title: Electroacupuncture at HT5 + GB20 produces stronger activation effect on swallowing cortex and muscle than single points
study.study_design: Three-group parallel randomized controlled trial with healthy subjects undergoing electroacupuncture at different acupoints
study.randomization: Subjects were randomly separated into three groups
study.population: 27 healthy subjects (15 males and 12 females), all right-handed and aged 22.4 ± 1.1 years
study.disease_condition: Healthy volunteers; study aimed to reveal mechanisms relevant to post-stroke swallowing dysphagia
study.exclusion_criteria: Severe pharyngitis, rhinitis, and other organic nasopharyngeal lesions, as well as throat or swallowing disorders; and diagnosis of brain damage, mental illness, or neck injury

conditions.timepoint_exact: first 10 s of resting state before test commencement
conditions.scan_context: fNIRS data from the first 10 s of resting state; electroacupuncture stimulation throughout

conditions.timepoint_exact: 15 s task periods across 4 cycles (total 4 x 15 s = 60 s of task data); electroacupuncture stimulation throughout
conditions.scan_context: Swallowing 3 mL of warm water task during electroacupuncture; fNIRS recording; 4 cycles of 35 s each

conditions.timepoint_exact: 20 s rest periods across 4 cycles; electroacupuncture stimulation throughout
conditions.scan_context: Subject remains quiet and avoids thinking and moving; fNIRS recording
Surface electromyography (sEMG) measurement of pharyngeal swallowing muscles after electroacupuncture

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: HT5 on both sides (palmar side of the forearm, at the radial edge of the ulnar carpal flexor tendon)
interventions.penetration_exact: 0.5 cun directly (main needle); 0.5 cun directly at the proximal end 0.2 cun close to the main needle (assistant needle for energization)
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 0.2–0.6 mA, enough to produce sensation in subjects
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Stay calm throughout the test, follow the movements as indicated, report any signs of discomfort; not to swallow, cough or vocalize at will
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: HT5 acupoint can clear the heart and help the tongue, treating tongue stiffness and speech; stimulates linguopharyngeal swallowing muscles

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: GB20 on both sides (in the collar, below the occipital bone, between the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles)
interventions.penetration_exact: obliquely 1 cun in the direction of the pharynx (main needle); 0.5 cun directly 0.2 cun from the proximal end of the main needle (assistant needle for energization only)
interventions.depth_exact: 1 cun oblique in direction of pharynx
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 0.2–0.6 mA, enough to produce sensation in subjects
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Stay calm throughout the test, follow the movements as indicated, report any signs of discomfort; not to swallow, cough or vocalize at will
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: GB20 point is a key point for dispersing all internal and external winds; acupuncture may dispel the winds and open the orifice to assist the throat; activates swallowing-related cerebral cortex

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: HT5 and GB20 on both sides
interventions.penetration_exact: same as respective single-point groups; two needles on the same side were linked
interventions.manipulation_exact: acupuncture to obtain Qi; the two needles on the same side were linked
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 0.2–0.6 mA, enough to produce sensation in subjects
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Stay calm throughout the test, follow the movements as indicated, report any signs of discomfort; not to swallow, cough or vocalize at will
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: The combination of the HT5 acupoints and the GB20 acupoints can treat post-stroke dysphagia from both central and peripheral perspectives; when two acupoints are electroacupunctured their effects superimpose resulting in more substantial central and peripheral activation impact

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: the intensity was adjusted between 0.2–0.6 mA, which was enough to produce sensation in subjects
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: The paper does not report formal deqi/sensation questionnaire data. The only sensory reference is that electrical intensity was sufficient to produce sensation.

extraction_notes.note: The study does not report individual group sample sizes explicitly (n per group). The total is 27 in a 1:1:1 ratio, implying n=9 per group, but this is inferred from the ratio statement rather than explicitly stated per group.

No formal deqi/sensation questionnaire (e.g., MASS, SAS, VAS) was administered. The only sensory reference is that electrical intensity was adjusted to 'produce sensation in subjects.' Sensory response data are not formally reported.
Blinding of participants, assessors, or statisticians is not described. The study does not report a sham control group.
Expectancy, credibility, and perceived treatment measures are not reported.

Exact numeric values for sEMG swallowing amplitudes per group (mean ± SD) are presented only in Fig. 5 and are not extractable from the figure with sufficient precision. Only statistical comparisons are reported in text.

Activation maps in Fig. 1A show topographic HbO2 changes across three conditions. Exact values per ROI are partially visible in Fig. 1B but only LM1 showed a statistically significant difference per text. Exact group means per non-significant ROIs are not reported in text.

The paper states the FC analysis used Pearson correlation coefficient on the 'oxygenation time series for each channel' and then Fisher r-to-z transformation. It is unclear whether the FC values in Table 1 are Pearson r values or Fisher z values. The paper refers to them as 'Pearson correlation coefficient' in the results section.

No MNI, Talairach, or any stereotaxic coordinates are reported. This is a fNIRS study using probe-based channel locations referenced to Brodmann areas and cortical surface locations, not a volumetric neuroimaging coordinate system.

The paper reports the HbO2 ANOVA result for LM1 as F = 4.043, P < 0.05, but does not report exact F or p values for the other seven ROIs that were not significant. It is unclear whether ANOVA was run on all 8 ROIs with only LM1 reaching significance, or only LM1 was tested.
The number of sessions is not reported. The experimental design implies a single session per subject, but this is not explicitly confirmed.

For the FC results, Table 1 reports RM1 and RS1, RM1 and LM1, RM1 and LS1, and RPM and LM1 as significant by ANOVA. However, the abstract mentions 'RM1 and RS1' but not 'RM1 and LS1' in the post-hoc comparisons between HT5+GB20 and GB20 group. Post-hoc results for RM1 and LS1 between groups are not reported in text beyond the ANOVA level.
The paper does not explicitly state n=9 per group; this is inferred from 'divided into three groups in a 1:1:1 ratio' with 27 total subjects.

The abstract states 'tighter FC in the RM1 and LM1 (t = 2.4629, P < 0.05)' referring to HT5+GB20 vs HT5, while the results section says the same. However, the abstract also mentions 'RM1 and RPM (t = 2.2116, P < 0.05)' in the HT5+GB20 vs GB20 comparison, which is consistent with results text. There is a minor discrepancy in the abstract where it says 'RPM' but Table 1 shows the comparison was RM1 and RPM; however the results text confirms this refers to the pair RM1-RPM.
